note: Checkpoint E6 baseline: single editable engine source + generated Node/add-on mirror + Worker/main-thread integration + final overlay. engine/source/plumline-engine.js is the ONE editable mathematical source. engine/engine.js is now a DERIVED artefact produced by engine/generate-engine-mirror.js from the canonical source + engine/source/engine-platform-adapter.json. E6 changes NO mathematics, NO algorithm, NO tolerance, NO status, NO stopReason, NO error, NO translation, NO UI, and the public output stays byte-identical. Current behaviours are COMPATIBILITY CHARACTERISATIONS, not endorsements.

mirror.status: GENERATED artefact (was hand-maintained). Derived deterministically from the canonical source by engine/generate-engine-mirror.js. Byte-identity with the old mirror was NOT maintainable: 11 functions carried independently-authored comments (~4583 bytes of comment divergence, e.g. detectModel_ 2046 chars) that cannot be derived from the canonical file in a maintainable way. The generated mirror is AST- and functionally equivalent to the old one: 88 top-level functions, all normalized-identical, same 20 exports in the same order, identical solveModel_ results (elapsedMs excluded). Only comments and formatting differ, hence the new SHA.
mirror.byte_identity_reason: 11 functions have independently-authored add-on comments (~4583 bytes) not derivable from the canonical source without embedding full comment blocks (which would duplicate platform text and be unmaintainable). Approved E6.4 path: new SHA + demonstrated AST/functional equivalence.

canonical_mirror_inventory.third_divergence: none — a third normalized-body divergence must fail the checker

constants_inventory.note: identical in canonical and generated mirror; a changed constant must fail

wrapper_contract.header: /* === Plumline engine: the exact same code as the Google Sheets add-on === */
wrapper_contract.no_engine_markers: the mirror carries NO ENGINE_START/ENGINE_END (standalone module, not a Worker slice)

generated_file_policy.verify_checks_freshness: npm run verify checks engine.js == generator output; it does NOT regenerate

separator.inserted_by: buildWorker(): new Blob([src + '\n' + glue]) — the single LF between engineSource and glue

worker_execution.engine_source_slice: engineSource() scans the page's <script> text for /* ENGINE_START */..indexOf(/* ENGINE_END */) and returns txt.slice(a,b): INCLUDES ENGINE_START, EXCLUDES ENGINE_END. Returns exactly the canonical bytes. Worker never reads engine/source, never fetches, never uses engine/engine.js, adds no request.

request_contract.note: postMessage payload from main thread to Worker; token added last (payload.token=myToken)

response_error_contract.note: {token, ok:false, phase, error}; phase is 'read' (detectModel_ threw) or 'solve'

token_contract.creation: workerToken starts at 0; each solve does myToken=++workerToken
token_contract.stale_guard: onmessage compares e.data.token !== workerToken (the GLOBAL, not captured myToken) and returns early; onerror compares myToken !== workerToken
token_contract.stale_effect: a stale response does not set lastResult, does not announce, does not plot, does not export, does not replace current errors; workerBusy stays as-is for the stale message
token_contract.cancel: cancel/edit does workerToken++ then terminate() + engineWorker=null (rebuild next time)

lifecycle_contract.build: buildWorker(): Blob([src + '\n' + glue], {type:'application/javascript'}); URL.createObjectURL; new Worker; URL.revokeObjectURL immediately after (code already loaded)
lifecycle_contract.success: onmessage: token guard, workerBusy=false, present result
lifecycle_contract.cleanup: terminate + engineWorker=null on cancel/replace so the next solve rebuilds; revokeObjectURL frees the Blob URL
lifecycle_contract.no_support: buildWorker sets engineWorker=false when Worker/Blob/URL unavailable -> main-thread fallback

fallback_contract.trigger: no Worker/Blob/URL support, or engine source not found -> engineWorker=false; solve() then uses solveMainThread()
fallback_contract.path: solveMainThread() -> setTimeout(runSolve,30); runSolve() calls detectModel_(sheet,lm) then solveModel_(sheet,model,lm) — the SAME composed canonical functions as the Worker, NOT engine/engine.js, no parser/solver reimplementation
fallback_contract.parity: Worker and fallback produce identical deterministic result fields (status/stopReason/optimalityProven/objective/values/nodesExplored/modelType); elapsedMs is the only non-comparable temporal field

error_routing_contract.engine_technical_error: thrown; Worker wraps as {ok:false, phase, error}; fallback catches in runSolve
error_routing_contract.infrastructure_error: Worker/Blob/postMessage/onerror failure -> engineWorker=false or terminate; distinct from an engine error
error_routing_contract.localization: localizeEngineError(msg) maps an engine error string to localized UI text; used on the Worker error path, the fallback/runSolve path, and solve — the engine never localizes
error_routing_contract.handoff: localizeEngineError stays in the UI layer; no error text or translation moved into the engine

suites_final.note: No suite depends on a SECOND editable mathematical source. engine/harness.js is now the explicit adapter for the GENERATED mirror (documented as a compatibility adapter, not the primary authority).

suite_migrations.note: The status-bearing legacy suites drive the generated mirror end-to-end via engine/harness.js. Their maths now traces to the single canonical source (the mirror is derived). They are kept as mirror-parity coverage; no case lost, no PASSED lost, no expected changed, no export added to the mirror to ease tests.
